notes: The parts come from one community teardown of the Revlon 1875W Compact Travel Hair Dryer, which prints no model code, so other Revlon 1875 W dryers may differ. The motor and fan are glued together and the teardown says the fan can't be removed without destroying it.

gaps: The teardown (title, device name, text) prints no model code, only 'Revlon 1875W Compact Travel Hair Dryer'; the record's id keeps RVDR5034 but the model name follows the teardown.
An Elitsac retailer page gives RVDR5034 as the model of a 'Revlon Essentials 1875W Black 2 Heat Compact Hair Dryer'; it does not mention the teardown, so the two are not tied.
Voltage, wattage and rpm of the motor and coils are not given by the teardown; the retailer's 120 V line is labelled AI-generated, so left out.
The teardown names no thermal cut-out, rectifier, circuit board or cord, so those template parts are not claimed.
method: iFixit teardown 'Revlon 1875W Compact Travel Hair Dryer Teardown' (guide 103582, community-written), read through the iFixit guide API and on the web page; no bot check. iFixit content is CC BY-NC-SA, used for facts and links only.
Elitsac product page for the Revlon Essentials 1875W 2 Heat Compact Hair Dryer opened to look for the RVDR5034 tie; not used as a source.
Walmart and Safeway listings showed bot checks and were not used; the manuals.plus page returned HTTP 403.

comps.spec: Hair dryer fan DC motor, yfd 385 2073 57 per the teardown. The impeller is glued onto its shaft.
7-fin PP impeller, tightly glued to the motor shaft. The teardown says the fan can't be replaced without destroying it.
Open heating coils, closely soldered with the motor. The teardown says two coils control the temperature.
3-position slide switch, TOPLY YSS-16-2413, for the High-Off-Low control.
comps.loc: In the handle section of the front case

comps.spec: Cold shot button, a TOPLY YSS-16 slide switch.
comps.loc: In the handle section of the front case
